entry.title: Build a presentation from source material
entry.summary: Create an editable deck that fits your audience and existing visual style.
prerequisites: Attach notes, data, or an existing deck; include the audience and any reference template.
entry.outcome: An editable presentation with checked layouts and clear review notes.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Create a presentation for [audience] that helps them [decision or outcome]. Use the attached material as the factual basis. Establish a concise narrative, then build the slides. If I supply a reference deck, preserve its layout conventions, typography, branding, and approved figures. Keep text and charts editable. Use visuals to explain the content and inspect every rendered slide for clipped text, crowded layouts, and misleading charts. Deliver the editable file and identify unsupported claims or content that needs my review.

steps.title: Adapt the audience
steps.prompt: Rework this deck for [new audience]. Change the level of detail and the explanation of the recommendation while retaining verified figures and the established visual style. Show which slides changed.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after reviewing the first result.

entry.title: Triage your inbox and draft replies
entry.summary: Find urgent email, suggest a cleanup, and prepare replies in your voice.
prerequisites: Connect the approved mailbox or provide an email export; include recent sent messages to establish tone.
entry.outcome: A prioritized inbox brief, cleanup proposal, and unsent reply drafts.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Review the last 90 days in [mailbox], including recent messages I wrote. Keep separate accounts separate. Identify up to five conversations that need action, with links, timing, and the reason each matters. Check the latest replies before calling a request unresolved. Propose labels and archive candidates without hiding bills, deadlines, security notices, or active conversations. Draft one useful response in my usual tone. End with separate decisions for applying the cleanup and saving the reply. Do not send messages, archive mail, or move anything to Trash until I approve the exact action.

steps.title: Set a review cadence
steps.prompt: Propose an inbox-check schedule for [time zone and working hours] using the priorities we agreed. Include the sources and notification rules in the task instructions. Show the schedule for approval, and confirm whether the platform can actually run it. Report meaningful changes without repeating resolved items.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after reviewing the first result.

entry.title: Complete a task across desktop apps
entry.summary: Use visible applications and local files to finish a clearly bounded task.
prerequisites: Requires a desktop agent with computer-control access and the relevant apps signed in.
entry.outcome: A completed task or a precise account of the remaining manual steps.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Help me complete [task] using [approved applications or folders]. Inspect the current screen and relevant files before acting. Follow the task across the necessary apps, verify the result in each destination, and summarize what changed. Ask before sending anything, making a purchase, confirming a booking, deleting data, or making another consequential change. If computer-control access is unavailable, tell me which steps I need to perform instead of claiming you completed them.

entry.title: Prioritize incoming bug reports
entry.summary: Combine scattered reports into one evidence-based engineering queue.
prerequisites: Provide the repository or service, time window, and approved issue, alert, log, or support sources.
entry.outcome: A deduplicated P0-P3 bug queue with evidence and next actions.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Triage reports for [service or team] from [time window]. Read [approved issue queues, error monitoring, support tickets, and discussion threads]. State which sources are inaccessible. Consolidate reports of the same underlying problem, then rank bugs from P0 to P3. Give each a concise title, observed evidence with links, impact, and the next diagnostic or remediation action. Distinguish a demonstrated failure from an untested hypothesis. If nothing qualifies, say so. Keep the review read-only: do not create tickets, change assignments, rerun jobs, post messages, or start fixes.

steps.title: Repeat the triage
steps.prompt: Draft recurring triage instructions using these sources, priority definitions, and duplicate rules. Include the proposed schedule and how to handle missing sources or an empty result. Keep the run read-only and show the configuration before scheduling it.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after reviewing the first result.

entry.title: Create a daily work briefing
entry.summary: Bring commitments, decisions, messages, and blockers into one concise view.
prerequisites: Connect or provide the relevant calendar, messages, email, documents, and project trackers.
entry.outcome: A source-linked briefing with the next decisions and actions.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Review my available work sources and prepare today's briefing. Establish my active projects, collaborators, commitments, and upcoming meetings. Prioritize changed deadlines, decisions I owe, unanswered messages, and work blocked on someone else. Check recent thread activity so resolved items do not resurface. Link every actionable item to its source, separate assumptions from confirmed facts, and name missing sources. Draft useful replies or meeting notes without sending or editing anything. Finish with the few actions that most need my attention today.

steps.title: Watch for meaningful changes
steps.prompt: Design an hourly check of the same approved sources. Notify me only when a decision, deadline, blocker, or message materially changes. Show the schedule and source access required; activate it only after approval and report if scheduling is unavailable.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after reviewing the first result.

entry.title: Benchmark a protein-folding hypothesis
entry.summary: Run controlled architecture experiments with durable records and comparable results.
prerequisites: Provide the model repository, NanoFold benchmark setup, scoring command, and compute limits.
entry.outcome: An experiment log with matched metrics, resource costs, and defensible conclusions.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Evaluate whether sparse higher-order geometric states improve this AlphaFold2-style model on NanoFold. Keep the usual MSA and residue-pair representations; investigate learned triplet faces and quadruplet tetrahedra using only official inputs and geometry recycled by the model. Track the strategy, experiments, and observations in durable files. For each iteration, state the hypothesis, make a bounded change, run the relevant tests and matched benchmark, and record lDDT-C-alpha, latency, memory, and failure modes. Decide whether to keep or revise the change. Do not present a smoke test or single-chain overfit as evidence of generalization.

entry.title: Build a refreshable sales dashboard
entry.summary: Explore sales trends with clear filters, calculations, and data-quality checks.
prerequisites: Provide a sales export or exact spreadsheet link; a dashboard-building environment is needed for implementation.
entry.outcome: A private dashboard with validated metrics and a documented refresh path.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Build a private dashboard from [sales file or exact spreadsheet link]. First inspect the columns, date range, missing rows, join keys, and inconsistent dates. Show revenue trends, customer segments, unusual changes, and useful date and segment filters. Explain the metric calculations and display the source's update date. Validate the charts against source totals. Prepare a refresh method that reads only the approved source and does not duplicate existing data. Show the working preview and unresolved data questions before sharing or publishing it.

steps.title: Monitor changes
steps.prompt: Propose a weekday refresh of this dashboard. Specify the source, comparison period, data-quality checks, and what would count as a meaningful change. Confirm scheduling and data access actually work before describing the dashboard as automatically updated.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after reviewing the first result.

entry.title: Find themes across product feedback
entry.summary: Combine customer signals into supported themes and concrete next steps.
prerequisites: Provide feedback exports or approved survey, support, issue, and discussion links.
entry.outcome: A theme-based feedback brief with supporting examples and draft follow-ups.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Analyze feedback about [product or feature] during [period] across the supplied support tickets, surveys, research notes, issues, and discussions. Group related concerns without losing the original context. Show supporting examples and source links for each theme, note disagreements, and distinguish recurring patterns from isolated reports. Identify the issues that need a product decision or further research. Return an editable brief or table and draft the follow-up questions; do not post messages or change the issue tracker.

steps.title: Develop a theme
steps.prompt: Take [reviewed theme] and draft the next useful artifact: an investigation brief, product requirement, or customer-response outline. Tie proposed changes to the actual feedback and list what still needs validation.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after reviewing the first result.

entry.title: Clean an inconsistent data export
entry.summary: Standardize formats and duplicates while preserving the original evidence.
prerequisites: Attach the CSV and identify its row IDs, date conventions, and known category aliases.
entry.outcome: A cleaned CSV plus an auditable record of uncertain and changed rows.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Clean [CSV file] without overwriting it. Resolve mixed date formats only where their meaning is clear. Normalize currency formatting but preserve missing amounts as blank. Identify repeat-export duplicates, standardize confirmed region and category aliases, and separate pasted summary rows from records. Keep source row IDs wherever possible. Return a new CSV and a data-quality note showing what changed, which rows were removed, and which values remain ambiguous. Do not fabricate replacements for missing or uncertain data.

entry.title: Compare drug-target evidence
entry.summary: Rank biological targets across independent research evidence streams.
prerequisites: Provide the disease, candidate targets, and access to relevant genetics, expression, literature, and clinical sources.
entry.outcome: A target-by-evidence matrix, ranked hypotheses, and explicit confidence limits.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Compare TSLP, IL33, and IL1RL1 as research targets for asthma. Review independent evidence from human genetics, cohort replication and PheWAS, disease associations, clinical precedent, literature, and tissue or cell-type expression. Score each target from 1 to 5 within each evidence stream using stated criteria. Separate direct asthma findings from related allergic conditions. Reconcile conflicting evidence and provide the overall ranking, confidence, and key limitations. Include a prioritization heatmap and a sourced summary of lead asthma-associated variants. Keep this a research prioritization exercise, not a treatment recommendation.

entry.title: Review single-cell RNA sequencing quality
entry.summary: Choose justified cell filters and inspect annotation patterns without losing raw counts.
prerequisites: Provide a 10x-style count-matrix bundle, sample manifest, dataset metadata, and an analysis runtime.
entry.outcome: A filtered h5ad file, QC tables, threshold plots, and a review summary.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Inspect the supplied single-cell count matrix, manifest, and metadata. Choose quality-control thresholds from the observed distributions rather than applying unexplained defaults. Preserve raw counts. Report the cells removed or flagged by each filter, show plots that justify the thresholds, and generate global and group-level UMAP views for review. Return the filtered h5ad dataset and a concise summary of quality issues, annotation uncertainty, and decisions that require scientific review. Do not imply that an attractive embedding validates the underlying labels.

entry.title: Validate bulk RNA sequencing inputs
entry.summary: Check reads, reference files, and sample quality before differential expression.
prerequisites: Provide sample sheet, FASTQ files, transcriptome and genome FASTA, GTF, and a configured bioinformatics runtime.
entry.outcome: A run manifest, QC report, count matrices, and a clear downstream-readiness assessment.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Run a documented FASTQ-to-count quality review using [sample sheet], [FASTQ folder], and the supplied reference FASTA and GTF files. Validate inputs and compute resources before starting. Produce a run manifest, MultiQC report, and Salmon transcript- and gene-level count matrices. Interpret mapping rates, duplication, expected versus observed library type, and outlier samples. Separate warnings from issues that block differential-expression analysis, and link every concern to its sample and evidence. Return usable report links and the output paths.

entry.title: Map future cash pressure
entry.summary: Build a formula-driven forecast that makes low-cash periods visible.
prerequisites: Attach cash balances, receipts, payment schedules, debt, tax, capex, and timing assumptions.
entry.outcome: An editable cash forecast with liquidity thresholds and visible assumptions.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Build a cash forecast for [business and horizon] from the supplied files. Retain their weekly or monthly cadence. Model opening cash, collections, payroll, suppliers, debt, taxes, capital spending, and working-capital timing using formulas and explicit assumptions. Flag missing timing information instead of hiding a guessed value. Highlight the lowest closing balance, when it occurs, and any breach of [minimum cash threshold]. Deliver an editable workbook whose assumptions I can change without rebuilding the calculations.

steps.title: Stress-test collections
steps.prompt: Model [collection delay or payment change] without changing the base case. Compare the lowest cash balance and threshold breaches, and identify which timing assumptions explain the difference.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after reviewing the first result.

entry.title: Turn multiple datasets into an answer
entry.summary: Clean, join, and analyze evidence with interpretable charts and limitations.
prerequisites: Attach datasets, define the question, and provide any known join keys or metric definitions.
entry.outcome: A reviewable report or notebook with validated joins and supporting charts.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Answer [research or business question] using the attached datasets. Explain what each file contains, establish valid join keys, and check duplicates, missing fields, unmatched records, and coverage. Preserve original files and do not fill gaps with invented data. Explore the question with clear charts and an interpretable model if needed. Lead the final report with the answer, then explain assumptions, uncertainty, and data problems that could change it. Distinguish association from causation and return the supporting workbook or notebook.

steps.title: Challenge the result
steps.prompt: Check whether the conclusion changes under a reasonable alternative join, outlier treatment, or model specification. Compare the results and explain which assumptions are consequential.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after reviewing the first result.

entry.title: Build a transparent DCF model
entry.summary: Connect operating assumptions to valuation in an editable workbook.
prerequisites: Attach company financials, approved assumptions, capital structure, and share count when available.
entry.outcome: A DCF workbook with operating drivers, valuation bridge, and clearly marked gaps.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Create a discounted cash-flow workbook for [company] using the supplied financials. Link revenue growth, margins, capital expenditure, and working capital to unlevered free cash flow. Calculate the discount rate, terminal value, and enterprise value transparently. Calculate equity and per-share values only when the source files supply the required capital structure and diluted share count; otherwise state which inputs are missing. Put missing assumptions in a labeled assumptions section; do not bury guesses in formulas. If full statements are unavailable, identify the limitation and model only the supported operating forecast. Deliver an editable XLSX.

steps.title: Audit the valuation before use
steps.instruction: Run this after building the workbook and before using its valuation outputs.
steps.prompt: Audit this DCF workbook against the source financials. Reconcile historical figures and distinguish formula-driven calculations from hardcoded inputs. Check operating drivers, unlevered free cash flow, WACC, terminal value, discounting, and the bridge from enterprise to equity value. Verify sensitivity-table formulas and their links to assumptions. Calculate per-share results only when the required capital structure and diluted share count are supplied. Identify errors, unsupported inputs, and exact cells requiring review; do not silently change business assumptions.

steps.title: Review sensitivity
steps.prompt: Show how enterprise and per-share value change with the discount rate and terminal-growth assumptions. Highlight unsupported inputs and formulas that deserve finance-owner review.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after reviewing the first result.

steps.title: Change one valuation assumption
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation with the specific assumption you want to change.
steps.prompt: Update only [assumption] to [new value] in the DCF workbook. Preserve the previous value in a visible change log, retain all other approved assumptions, and recalculate linked outputs and sensitivity tables. Report which tabs and valuation results changed, including the size of the impact. Flag any dependency or missing input that prevents a valid recalculation rather than making unrelated adjustments.

entry.title: Explain budget variances
entry.summary: Map actuals to plan and distinguish favorable from unfavorable movements.
prerequisites: Attach actuals, budget categories, the chart of accounts, and reporting-period definitions.
entry.outcome: An editable variance workbook with reconciled categories and clear exceptions.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Compare [period] actuals with the approved budget in a new workbook. Map accounts to the correct budget categories, preserving the raw imports and flagging ambiguous mappings. Use formulas for amount and percentage differences. Interpret the direction by account type: additional revenue and additional expense have different implications. Summarize the material movements and identify source gaps or owner questions. Keep unmatched categories visible instead of forcing them into a convenient bucket.

steps.title: Check the explanation
steps.prompt: Reconcile the largest variances to their source accounts. Distinguish timing effects, volume or rate changes, and unsupported explanations; list the questions needed to resolve the latter.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after reviewing the first result.

entry.title: Review a pull request for regressions
entry.summary: Find consequential behavior changes, security risks, and missing coverage.
prerequisites: Provide the pull request or exact diff and repository context.
entry.outcome: Severity-ranked findings with code references and verification gaps.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Review [pull request or diff] against its base revision. Focus on regressions, security-relevant behavior changes, data loss, and tests that fail to cover the changed contract. Trace affected callers and error paths before raising a finding. For each actionable issue, explain the concrete trigger, impact, and relevant file and line. Put findings first by severity. State what was verified and which checks were not run. If no issues are supported by evidence, say so without implying the change is fully proven safe.

entry.title: Run a focused repository security review
entry.summary: Assess a defined code scope and report realistic risks with evidence.
prerequisites: Requires an authorized repository, security guidance, and a code-capable environment.
entry.outcome: A security report covering findings, proof, exclusions, and gaps.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Assess [repository or scoped folder] for security vulnerabilities. I am authorized to review this code. Read its security policy and architecture context, stay inside the named scope, and use supported validation methods. Trace plausible findings to affected code and realistic impact. Separate validated issues from unresolved suspicions. Report severity, evidence, assumptions, reviewed surfaces, exclusions, and remaining coverage gaps. Prioritize the findings and uncertainties that need human review. Do not apply patches or close findings during this assessment.

steps.title: Understand one finding
steps.prompt: Explain [finding] from attacker-controlled input to the broken security boundary. Identify the prerequisites, evidence that supports the impact, and the smallest validation needed to resolve uncertainty.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after reviewing the first result.

entry.title: Create a native Mac app workspace
entry.summary: Build a SwiftUI shell with coordinated navigation, inspector, menus, and settings.
prerequisites: Requires a macOS development environment, Xcode, and an app brief or existing repository.
entry.outcome: A working Mac app shell with native controls and reproducible build steps.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Build a Mac-native SwiftUI shell for [app]. Use a main WindowGroup and a separate Settings scene. Coordinate a lightweight sidebar, detail view, and inspector with explicit selection state. Put primary actions in menus, toolbars, and keyboard shortcuts. Use window-scoped storage for navigation and app storage for preferences. Prefer semantic colors and native materials; introduce an AppKit bridge only for a specific behavior SwiftUI cannot express. Add a reusable build-and-run script, exercise the main navigation and preferences, and report the exact verification commands.

entry.title: Implement a responsive design reference
entry.summary: Translate screenshots into the existing product without inventing a second design system.
prerequisites: Provide screenshots, interaction notes, and access to the current frontend repository and browser preview.
entry.outcome: A responsive implementation checked against the reference at multiple screen sizes.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Implement [screen or flow] from the attached screenshots and notes in this repository. Reuse its components, tokens, routing, state, and data-fetching conventions. Match the visual hierarchy, spacing, proportions, and responsive behavior. Resolve ambiguous details with the simplest choice consistent with the reference and record the assumption. Check the finished page in a real browser at desktop and mobile widths, exercise its interactions, and correct observed differences before delivery.

steps.title: Refine one detail
steps.prompt: Adjust [specific mismatch] to match the reference. Recheck the affected desktop and mobile layouts and confirm that the interaction still works.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after reviewing the first result.

entry.title: Map an unfamiliar code path
entry.summary: Trace ownership, validation, and data flow before making a change.
prerequisites: Provide the repository and the feature, request, or subsystem to investigate.
entry.outcome: A source-linked flow explanation and a prioritized reading path.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Trace how [request or feature] moves through this codebase, from entry point to response or persisted result. Explain which modules own each step, where inputs are validated, and where authentication, side effects, and error handling occur. Cite the actual files and symbols. Highlight important invariants and likely pitfalls for a developer changing this flow. Finish with the smallest useful set of files to read next. Keep observations separate from assumptions where runtime evidence is missing.

entry.title: Plan a defensive AI access rollout
entry.summary: Prepare a controlled access plan and verify that approved users can use the required security capability.
prerequisites: Provide the security-access program, current official setup guide, workspace state, and approved member list.
entry.outcome: An owner-reviewed rollout checklist with access verification and unresolved requirements.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Prepare an access-rollout checklist for [approved defensive security program] in [workspace]. Use the current official instructions and the workspace evidence I provide. Separate pending application or verification from active access. Identify the authorized owner, approved members, required model permissions, role or group assignments, and how to check for unintended access through other roles. Treat API-project access as a separate setup when applicable. Propose a small benign verification task for an approved user and document troubleshooting checks. Do not submit attestations, change roles, or grant access; return the concrete steps for owner review.

entry.title: Configure automatic pull-request security reviews
entry.summary: Choose review triggers and reporting thresholds suited to repository risk.
prerequisites: Provide repository access, supported security-review tooling, and current configuration documentation.
entry.outcome: A review configuration proposal with sensitive-path overrides and a validation plan.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Review the security-review options for [repository] using its current tooling documentation. Propose when automatic and manually requested reviews should run, which severity levels should be reported, and which sensitive paths need tighter thresholds. Consider authentication, authorization, payment, infrastructure, and dependency code separately from low-risk areas. Explain the difference between ordinary correctness review and security analysis. Show the proposed settings, expected pull-request output, and a controlled verification change before altering repository configuration.

entry.title: Triage dependency risk in CI
entry.summary: Connect package alerts to reachable code and review dependency updates.
prerequisites: Provide dependency alerts, manifests, lockfiles, CI configuration, and authorized repository access.
entry.outcome: A dependency-risk ledger and a narrowly scoped scan workflow proposal.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Assess [dependency alerts or package update] against this repository. Check the affected versions, whether the vulnerable behavior is reachable, and what evidence supports or weakens each alert. Produce a ledger with validated, unresolved, and ruled-out findings and reasons. Propose a CI check triggered by relevant manifest or lockfile changes. Keep runner credentials isolated, handle untrusted pull requests appropriately, and preserve scan reports even on failure. Do not run package lifecycle scripts or dismiss alerts merely because a scanner completed.

entry.title: Inspect security risks in a local code change
entry.summary: Review the working diff with its surrounding repository context.
prerequisites: Provide the local checkout, intended change set, and security guidance.
entry.outcome: A focused diff review with affected lines, realistic impact, and remaining uncertainty.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Inspect the current changes in [repository] for security regressions. Confirm which edits belong to the intended task and identify the comparison revision. Read enough surrounding code to understand authorization, validation, and data handling affected by the patch. Report supported findings with exact locations, triggering conditions, and evidence; distinguish them from questions that need runtime validation. Keep unrelated work untouched and do not apply fixes as part of this review.

entry.title: Write useful security review context
entry.summary: Document the system boundaries and reporting rules reviewers need.
prerequisites: Provide architecture documents, repository instructions, security expectations, and known limitations.
entry.outcome: A draft threat model and security policy grounded in the actual application.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Inspect [repository] and the supplied architecture material. Draft a threat model describing protected assets, entry points, untrusted inputs, trust boundaries, privileged operations, and authentication assumptions. Separately draft SECURITY.md guidance defining security invariants, reportable findings, severity context, and exclusions. Keep engineering workflow instructions in their existing home and link supporting documents as a knowledge base. Cite code or source evidence, mark assumptions for owner review, and include known limitations rather than inventing controls. Present the proposed documents before committing them.

entry.title: Prepare and verify a security patch
entry.summary: Move a reviewed finding through a focused patch and evidence-based verification.
prerequisites: Provide the reviewed finding, affected repository, reproduction evidence, and supported test commands.
entry.outcome: A focused patch, before-and-after evidence, and a draft review description.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Address [reviewed finding] in this repository. Confirm the vulnerable behavior and the legitimate behavior that must remain. Prepare the smallest focused patch with a regression test or repeatable validation artifact. Show the proposed diff before applying it when the review workflow supports that separation. Verify that the original issue no longer occurs and normal behavior still works; record exact commands and limitations. Prepare a review description linking the finding, code changes, and evidence. Do not close the finding, merge, or deploy solely because a patch was generated.

entry.title: Turn a discussion thread into a code fix
entry.summary: Investigate a reported issue using its conversation context and the correct repository.
prerequisites: Provide the discussion thread, repository, and prepared development environment.
entry.outcome: A minimal fix with checks and a draft response to the original discussion.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Investigate the issue described in [thread] for [repository]. Use the approved development environment and read the repository instructions. Extract the expected behavior and concrete failure evidence from the discussion, inspect the relevant code, and make the smallest supported fix. Run the checks that cover the change and report any reproduction or access gaps. Prepare a concise response explaining the cause, change, and verification. Keep the response as a draft unless I explicitly authorize posting it.

entry.title: Prepare a new-hire onboarding packet
entry.summary: Stage readiness trackers and welcome materials using approved hiring information.
prerequisites: Provide the approved new-hire roster, start-date window, manager mapping, tracker template, and announcement/privacy rules.
entry.outcome: A staged tracker update, readiness-gap list, and private welcome plan.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Prepare onboarding drafts for accepted hires starting during [date range]. Use only [approved roster and mapping sources]. Check source fields and group hires by team and manager; flag missing role, start date, work contact, buddy, location, or equipment/account readiness. Propose tracker updates and a team summary. Draft welcome-space names, membership, and messages only within the approved announcement and privacy rules. Exclude compensation, identity documents, medical details, interview notes, and other unrelated sensitive information. Return the staged rows and exact drafts for review without changing HR records, inviting people, creating channels, or sending messages.

steps.title: Review readiness gaps
steps.prompt: Prioritize the missing onboarding information by what blocks the start date. For each gap, identify the appropriate owner from the approved mapping and draft a minimal clarification request without exposing the full roster.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after reviewing the first result.

entry.title: Run a deep repository security assessment
entry.summary: Use repeated investigation passes to reduce missed vulnerabilities and clarify coverage.
prerequisites: Requires authorized repository access, a security-capable code agent, and an explicit assessment scope.
entry.outcome: A consolidated security report with validated findings and remaining proof gaps.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Perform a deep security assessment of [repository or exact folder]. Read the security policy and preserve the agreed scope. Use independent discovery passes across relevant surfaces, consolidate duplicates, and validate the strongest candidates against their actual source-to-impact paths. Keep evidence and coverage records for each pass. Report surviving findings, realistic exploit prerequisites, reviewed areas, exclusions, and proof gaps. Distinguish this repository-wide assessment from a pull-request diff review. Do not apply fixes or imply that incomplete coverage establishes security.

entry.title: Convert a customer meeting into follow-ups
entry.summary: Draft consistent customer, account, and internal updates from meeting evidence.
prerequisites: Provide the meeting transcript, summary, account context, and intended destinations.
entry.outcome: A source-backed meeting recap and separate unsent follow-up drafts.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Use [customer meeting transcript and summary] to identify decisions, risks, opportunities, and explicit commitments with owners and dates. Name any missing source before drafting. Prepare a customer follow-up email, an account-plan update, CRM notes, and an internal team message. Ground important claims in the transcript and keep internal-only information out of the customer version. Flag uncertain ownership or timing instead of inventing commitments. Return the drafts separately; do not create records, assign work, send email, or post messages.

steps.title: Compare recurring calls
steps.prompt: Compare this call with the previous three. Highlight new decisions, changed commitments, emerging risks, and unresolved actions. Update the drafts only where the evidence changed and flag missing transcripts.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after reviewing the first result.

entry.title: Learn a research concept from its evidence
entry.summary: Build a study guide that separates a paper's claims from established knowledge.
prerequisites: Provide the paper or accessible link and describe your current background.
entry.outcome: A cited learning report with a glossary, diagrams, limitations, and study questions.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Help me understand [concept] using [research paper]. Examine its problem, contribution, methods, experiments, figures, and limitations. Explain the prerequisite terms I need and distinguish what the paper demonstrates from its claims and your interpretation. Build a concise learning report with a glossary, method walkthrough, concept map, evidence table, caveats, and open questions. Cite sections, pages, or figures. Use diagrams where they clarify the mechanism; do not add unverified scientific detail.

steps.title: Practice the concept
steps.prompt: Design a small reproducible example that illustrates one mechanism in the paper. Explain the inputs, expected output, and limitations, then provide a runnable script or notebook with a chart or table I can inspect.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after reviewing the first result.

entry.title: Turn an idea into a working prototype
entry.summary: Explore a visual direction and implement the core user journey.
prerequisites: Provide the idea, audience, main workflow, and a development environment; image generation is optional for visual exploration.
entry.outcome: A working first version with browser-checked interactions.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Develop a proof of concept for [idea] aimed at [users]. Define the main workflow and create a visual mockup that makes the direction concrete. Use that reference to implement a focused working version in the available project. Preserve the chosen visual hierarchy and make the primary interaction complete. Check it in a real browser, report what is simulated or missing, and provide the local run instructions.

steps.title: Iterate on feedback
steps.prompt: Apply [specific feedback] to the prototype. Keep the change focused, exercise the affected browser flow, and compare the result with the chosen design before handing it back.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after reviewing the first result.

entry.title: Prepare a web app preview deployment
entry.summary: Build the requested site and verify a reviewable deployment.
prerequisites: Provide source code or a brief, required assets, and an authorized deployment account.
entry.outcome: A verified preview URL with build results and remaining limitations.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Build or update [website] using [repository, screenshots, or brief]. Follow [product and style constraints] and preserve [unchanged areas]. Complete the required interactions, run the local build, and inspect the result. Using the approved hosting connection, deploy a preview and verify that the deployment is ready before returning its URL. If hosting access is unavailable, return the working local version and exact missing setup rather than claiming a deployment succeeded.

entry.title: Resolve a reported vulnerability
entry.summary: Turn an accepted external or internal finding into a minimal, testable remediation.
prerequisites: Provide the report, affected component, expected security invariant, proof, and repository access.
entry.outcome: A focused remediation with reproduction evidence and regression coverage.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Fix [accepted security finding] from [report or ticket]. Review the attacker-controlled input, broken control, expected invariant, and existing proof. Confirm the issue still exists when feasible; if it is already fixed, show the evidence. Make the smallest change that restores the invariant, add a focused regression check, and verify both the original failure and legitimate behavior. Keep unrelated findings and refactors out of scope. Return changed files, commands, results, and any remaining uncertainty without merging or deploying.

entry.title: Check a diff for security regressions
entry.summary: Trace security-sensitive changes against an exact base and head.
prerequisites: Provide an authorized PR, commit range, or working-tree diff and its security context.
entry.outcome: A security diff report with evidence-backed findings and review locations.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Review [exact pull request, commit range, or patch] for security regressions. Confirm the revisions and focus on [sensitive surfaces]. Trace changed input handling, authorization, secrets, filesystem, network, and dependency behavior into surrounding code where relevant. For each finding, explain a realistic trigger and impact with precise code references and validation evidence. Keep uncertainty explicit and identify coverage gaps. Return a Markdown review and suggested inline comments; do not silently expand the task into a full repository audit.

entry.title: Assess exposure to a dependency advisory
entry.summary: Determine whether a public package incident actually affects your repository.
prerequisites: Provide the advisory URL, repository, lockfiles, and relevant CI or build configuration.
entry.outcome: An exposure assessment with repository evidence and a proposed remediation path.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Evaluate [public package advisory] against this repository using read-only inspection. Establish affected packages and versions from authoritative sources. Inspect manifests, lockfiles, CI permissions, lifecycle scripts, and relevant built or vendored artifacts. Explain what proves exposure and what would rule it out, including token or cache implications when relevant. Classify the result as confirmed, unresolved, or ruled out, with file references and impact limits. Do not install packages, execute lifecycle scripts, rotate credentials, or delete files.

steps.title: Plan remediation
steps.prompt: For confirmed exposure, propose the exact package or configuration changes, verification, rollback, and any credential review required. Keep commands that execute untrusted code out of the plan unless their safety is established.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after reviewing the first result.

entry.title: Test the app as a real user
entry.summary: Exercise important flows and capture actionable reproduction details.
prerequisites: Provide the test environment, approved account or fixtures, and the critical user flows.
entry.outcome: A prioritized bug report with expected and actual results.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Test [application or environment] through these user journeys: [flows]. Navigate the real interface, including relevant forms, empty states, and transitions. For each failure, record reproducible steps, expected behavior, actual behavior, severity, and useful screenshots or logs. Continue past non-blocking issues so the review covers all requested flows. Finish with a triage summary and state what could not be tested. Use only the approved test data and avoid consequential production actions.

entry.title: Modernize an AI API integration
entry.summary: Upgrade the supported API path while preserving application behavior.
prerequisites: Provide the repository, provider, current integration, target requirements, and access to official documentation.
entry.outcome: A bounded migration with updated prompts, tests, and compatibility notes.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Inspect this [AI provider] integration and inventory models, endpoints, tool contracts, response handling, and prompt assumptions. Consult current official documentation for the supported migration path and model-specific prompting guidance. Propose the smallest upgrade that meets [requirements], then implement it within the approved scope. Preserve observable behavior unless the new API requires a change. Test tool calls and response shapes, and explicitly flag manual review points or unsupported features. Do not assume a model-name substitution is a complete migration.

entry.title: Act on a request found in messages
entry.summary: Follow a conversation into the necessary apps and prepare a contextual reply.
prerequisites: Provide the message thread and approved app access; execution requires an agent that can operate those apps.
entry.outcome: The completed bounded task and an unsent reply in context.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Read the messages from [person or thread] and establish exactly what was requested. Check later replies for changes or resolution. Complete the authorized task using [approved applications], verifying the result at the destination. Draft a reply that explains the outcome in the original conversation's tone. Pause before a purchase, booking, deletion, external commitment, or any other irreversible action. If required access is missing, describe the remaining steps precisely instead of claiming completion.

entry.title: Build an interface from a Figma frame
entry.summary: Implement the exact design variant using your existing frontend conventions.
prerequisites: Provide the Figma file and exact frame or node, repository access, and a browser preview.
entry.outcome: A responsive screen matched to the selected design and tested in the browser.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Implement [Figma frame] in this project. Retrieve the frame's design context and screenshot first; if the response is too large, inspect its structure and fetch only the required nodes. Reuse existing components, tokens, assets, routes, and state patterns. Match layout, spacing, typography, and responsive behavior rather than substituting a generic design. Use the provided image and vector assets where available. Compare the implemented result with the exact design variant in desktop and mobile browser views, and verify the key interactions.

steps.title: Check design fidelity
steps.prompt: Review the implementation against [frame or updated screenshot]. List visible differences by impact, fix the approved discrepancies, and recheck responsive behavior and interactions.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after reviewing the first result.

entry.title: Prototype a playable browser game
entry.summary: Build and playtest the core loop before expanding the game.
prerequisites: Provide the game concept, controls, target devices, and a runnable development repository.
entry.outcome: A playable browser game with run instructions and a record of playtest results.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Plan and build a browser game about [concept] in this repository. Define the core loop, controls, win or loss conditions, and first playable scope in a short plan. Create the required visuals and implement the game with a coherent interface. Keep a work log as you iterate. Run it in a real browser, play the complete loop, and inspect input handling, restart behavior, and layout on the target devices. Fix observed problems and return the run command, playtest evidence, and known limitations.

entry.title: Package a repeatable workflow as a skill
entry.summary: Capture a proven process with reusable instructions, commands, and output expectations.
prerequisites: Provide a successful example, supporting runbook or thread, reusable commands, and the target agent platform.
entry.outcome: A reusable skill grounded in a demonstrated workflow.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Create a reusable agent skill for [recurring task]. Learn from [successful example] and [runbook, review, or discussion]. Identify the inputs, sequence, decision points, reusable scripts, validation commands, and expected output. Preserve the important behavior from the working example while removing one-off details. Make instructions specific enough for another run to follow and clearly state when the skill applies. Verify its format against the target platform and test it with a representative task rather than inventing untested capabilities.

entry.title: Improve a difficult task through evaluation
entry.summary: Use scored iterations and direct artifact review to reach a measurable target.
prerequisites: Provide the workspace, scoring command, target metrics, and practical runtime limits.
entry.outcome: The best evaluated result, iteration history, and remaining weaknesses.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Improve [task] through a measured iteration loop. Read the workspace instructions and locate the existing evaluation command before changing anything. Record the baseline. Make one focused improvement, rerun the evaluation, and inspect the resulting artifact directly. Log what changed, scores, and observed tradeoffs. Continue toward [target thresholds] within [resource limits], keeping changes only when evidence supports them. Do not optimize a score while ignoring a visibly worse result. Return the strongest version, major iterations, bottlenecks, and unresolved risks.

entry.title: Write a business performance review
entry.summary: Connect KPI changes and financial results into a source-backed leadership narrative.
prerequisites: Provide KPI definitions, close and forecast workbooks, prior reviews, and owner commentary.
entry.outcome: An editable business review with cited numbers, anomalies, and owner questions.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Prepare the [period] performance review for [business or team] using only the supplied dashboards, financial tables, forecasts, prior review, and owner notes. Lead with the decisions and material changes leadership needs to understand. Explain key variances, anomalies, forecast changes, risks, and data-quality concerns with supporting charts where useful. Cite the exact source behind material figures. List missing inputs and unsupported explanations explicitly, and assign follow-up questions only where an owner is identified. Return an editable document for review.

steps.title: Audit the narrative
steps.prompt: Check every material number and causal explanation against its source. Mark unsupported claims, reconcile inconsistent figures, and tighten the leadership summary without concealing uncertainty.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after reviewing the first result.

entry.title: Refresh a leadership reporting deck
entry.summary: Update the story across workstreams while preserving the established deck.
prerequisites: Provide the previous deck, initiative tracker, KPI and forecast inputs, cash view, and leadership notes.
entry.outcome: An editable reporting deck with source tie-outs, visual checks, and review flags.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Refresh the [period] leadership reporting pack using the prior deck and supplied financial, initiative, and owner updates. Identify the common story across workstreams, then update metrics, deltas, charts, risks, milestones, and decisions. Preserve the deck's visual system. Trace significant numbers to source files and flag figures that do not reconcile or require owner confirmation. Render the finished slides and correct overflow, clipping, and layout issues. Deliver the editable presentation and a short list of changes and leadership review points; do not share it.

steps.title: Review changes
steps.prompt: Compare the revised pack with the previous version. Identify changed conclusions, revised figures, new risks, and slides that depend on unresolved assumptions or owner input.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after reviewing the first result.

entry.title: Prepare an evidence-based meeting brief
entry.summary: Arrive with the objective, context, agenda, and decisions clearly organized.
prerequisites: Provide the meeting date, calendar event, and specific notes, documents, or threads to consult.
entry.outcome: A concise meeting brief with sources, questions, and a notes template.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Prepare me for [meeting] on [date]. Use only [named calendar event, documents, notes, and discussion threads]. Start by confirming accessible sources and identifying gaps. Explain the meeting objective, relevant attendee context, facts we should share, likely agenda, unresolved questions, and decisions or commitments I may owe. Link to supporting evidence. Add a practical notes template for decisions and follow-ups. Put unsupported assumptions in a separate section. Do not send messages, edit shared notes, or distribute the brief.

steps.title: Shorten the pre-read
steps.prompt: Condense this into a one-page pre-read with the objective, three essential facts, decisions needed, and the most consequential open questions. Retain source links.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after reviewing the first result.

entry.title: Keep product documentation aligned with code
entry.summary: Update the public guidance affected by a real implementation change.
prerequisites: Provide changed source files, relevant docs, release context, and documentation validation commands.
entry.outcome: A focused documentation update with verified claims and preserved cross-links.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Update documentation for [feature] from the changed code, current docs, and supplied issue or release references. Establish what actually changed for users. Revise only the affected pages while preserving terminology, structure, and links. Keep private customer information, internal-only notes, and unpublished plans out of public content. Check examples and claims against the implementation, run the relevant documentation checks, and summarize the changes, verification, and any unresolved mismatch.

steps.title: Make future updates repeatable
steps.prompt: Document the source files, documentation pages, and checks that should be reviewed together for future changes to this feature. Propose a narrow recurring check without automatically publishing edits.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after reviewing the first result.

entry.title: Build an iPhone and iPad app slice
entry.summary: Create or extend a SwiftUI app with a repeatable build-and-launch loop.
prerequisites: Requires macOS, Xcode, the target simulator, and an app brief or existing project.
entry.outcome: A working iOS feature slice with exact build and verification instructions.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Build [iPhone or iPad app feature] in this project. First determine whether this is a new scaffold or an existing Xcode application. Reuse established models, navigation, and utilities. Choose the correct scheme and simulator, use xcodebuild or the available Xcode automation, and add a small build-and-launch script. Validate each meaningful change with the narrowest useful check before broader builds. Deliver the working feature, exact commands and environment used, and any unverified device-specific behavior.

entry.title: Assess security across a repository portfolio
entry.summary: Keep each repository's revision, findings, and coverage independently traceable.
prerequisites: Provide authorized repository URLs, full commit SHAs, scan tooling, and approved concurrency and cost limits.
entry.outcome: A per-repository assessment ledger with separate evidence and follow-up actions.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Prepare and run an authorized security assessment for [repository inventory]. Require a unique ID and full commit SHA for every repository; do not silently substitute a branch tip or uncommitted state. Use the approved concurrency, scan mode, and estimated cost limits. Save private results separately for each repository outside the scanned trees. Verify the scanned revisions, completion status, findings, and coverage gaps. Distinguish successful execution from an absence of vulnerabilities. Return a portfolio ledger of investigations, accepted fixes, and incomplete coverage, with the evidence paths and safe resume instructions.

entry.title: Explain a KPI movement
entry.summary: Break a metric change into supported drivers and testable hypotheses.
prerequisites: Provide the metric definition, date window, source exports, segment cuts, and relevant launch or campaign context.
entry.outcome: A root-cause brief with reconciled changes, charts, and next investigations.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Investigate why [KPI] changed during [period]. Confirm the metric definition and compare the relevant periods using the supplied source data. Break the change down by useful cohorts, channels, regions, segments, or product surfaces. Quantify the largest contributions and relate them to known events without treating correlation as proof. Separate confirmed drivers from hypotheses, flag data-quality issues, and cite the evidence. Return charts, open questions, and recommended next checks without altering the source.

steps.title: Challenge the cause
steps.prompt: Test the leading explanation against alternative segments, timing, or measurement changes. Identify the strongest evidence against it and the additional data needed to resolve the question.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after reviewing the first result.

entry.title: Specify a dashboard that supports decisions
entry.summary: Define metrics, views, ownership, and monitoring before building.
prerequisites: Provide the business question, workflow, metric definitions, source examples, and stakeholder needs.
entry.outcome: A buildable dashboard specification with validation and ownership rules.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Design a dashboard specification for [workflow or decision]. Use the supplied strategy, data exports, metric definitions, existing examples, and feedback. Explain the decisions it should enable, the KPI hierarchy, each calculation, chart, and filter, and the data needed. Define quality checks, acceptance checks, owners, handoffs, and a monitoring approach. Highlight access and publication constraints. Do not invent a metric definition or call the design production-ready before its sources and calculations are validated.

steps.title: Define actionable alerts
steps.prompt: For each proposed monitored metric, specify the threshold or comparison, owner, required context, and expected response. Remove alerts that have no useful decision or reliable source behind them.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after reviewing the first result.

entry.title: Report an initiative's current health
entry.summary: Show material progress, blockers, and decisions without rewriting the tracker.
prerequisites: Provide initiative documents, tracker, prior update, KPI changes, decision log, and owner notes.
entry.outcome: A concise initiative update that separates confirmed status from inference.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Prepare the [weekly or monthly] update for [initiative]. Compare the current tracker, metrics, decisions, and owner notes with the previous brief. Focus on material progress and changes, blockers, dependencies, decisions needed, and the next actions with supported owners. Identify stale items that need confirmation. Link important claims to evidence and distinguish inferred status from explicit updates. Return a reviewable brief without editing the project tracker or sending it.

steps.title: Compare reporting periods
steps.prompt: Show what changed between [previous period] and [current period]: completed milestones, shifted dates, resolved or new blockers, and changed decisions. Exclude unchanged background.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after reviewing the first result.

entry.title: Choose the accounts that need attention
entry.summary: Rank account work by urgency, risk, upside, and evidence.
prerequisites: Provide account exports, recent conversations, usage signals, account plans, and prioritization criteria.
entry.outcome: A ranked account focus list with grounded next actions.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Prioritize [number] accounts for [renewal, growth, or pipeline objective] this week. Use the supplied account records, recent calls, open email threads, usage data, and review criteria. For each account, explain why it matters now, the strongest risk or opportunity, the next useful action, and the source evidence. Flag stale or missing context that could change the ranking. Draft follow-up notes only where the next step is clear. Do not update the CRM or contact customers.

steps.title: Adjust the priorities
steps.prompt: Re-rank the list using [changed criterion or capacity]. Explain which accounts moved and why, keeping the evidence and uncertainty visible.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after reviewing the first result.

entry.title: Pressure-test a sales forecast
entry.summary: Separate reliable commitments from upside and deals that need to move out.
prerequisites: Provide opportunity exports, forecast snapshots, calls, legal or procurement status, and owner notes.
entry.outcome: A deal-by-deal forecast recommendation with evidence and follow-up questions.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Review [deals] for the [period] forecast. Reconcile current opportunity records with recent calls, messages, usage signals, support issues, and legal or procurement progress. Recommend which deals belong in commit, upside, or outside this period. Explain each recommendation using sourced facts and clearly labeled inference. Identify blockers, stale assumptions, missing evidence, and owner follow-ups for the forecast call. Keep the CRM and official forecast unchanged.

steps.title: Prepare the forecast discussion
steps.prompt: Turn the highest-risk recommendations into a short call agenda. For each deal, state the decision needed, the evidence to confirm, and the question its owner should answer.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after reviewing the first result.

entry.title: Coordinate a student team project
entry.summary: Bring milestones, owners, budget, decisions, and communication into one plan.
prerequisites: Provide project notes, member availability, budget, campus rules, and deadlines.
entry.outcome: A proposed project hub and reviewable operating materials.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Organize [club, event, or team project] using the shared notes, budget, member availability, campus requirements, and deadlines. Propose a clear folder structure, milestones, owner tracker, budget sheet, next-meeting agenda, communications drafts, and a decision/risk log. Link important requirements to their source and flag unresolved choices. Keep owner assignments and external communication as proposals until the team approves them; do not reorganize files or send messages without agreement.

entry.title: Scope an ambiguous analytics request
entry.summary: Translate a stakeholder question into a defensible analysis and first answer.
prerequisites: Provide the original request, relevant context, metric definitions, and available data sources.
entry.outcome: An analysis plan, first-pass result, and a list of decisions still needed.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Turn [stakeholder request] into a concrete analysis. Define the decision to support, business question, relevant metrics, required data, join logic, and scope. Identify unclear definitions before calculating. Run a first pass only where the available data supports it, validate outputs, and prepare a concise answer with charts, caveats, and sources. List every missing input or unresolved decision that prevents a final conclusion. Do not assume missing values or silently choose conflicting metric definitions.

steps.title: Respond to the requester
steps.prompt: Draft a short stakeholder response with the provisional answer, what can be concluded now, and the few clarifications that would materially improve the analysis. Keep it as a draft.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after reviewing the first result.

entry.title: Write a decision memo from research
entry.summary: Compare evidence, alternatives, costs, and uncertainty in one reviewable recommendation.
prerequisites: Provide the decision, research sources, internal context, budget limits, and decision criteria.
entry.outcome: A concise decision memo with traceable evidence and explicit tradeoffs.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Help [team] decide whether to [decision]. Use the supplied research, planning documents, models, stakeholder notes, and budget constraints. Apply [decision criteria] to the alternatives. Recommend a path with supporting evidence, costs, risks, tradeoffs, unresolved questions, and required owner confirmations. Keep any requested external research distinct from internal evidence. Link material claims to sources and record the assumptions that could change the recommendation. Produce a reviewable memo and supporting pre-read without making the decision or sharing it.

steps.title: Pressure-test the recommendation
steps.prompt: Argue the strongest evidence-based case for the leading alternative. Identify what new evidence or changed assumption would reverse the recommendation and revise the decision memo accordingly.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after reviewing the first result.

entry.title: Explain why an initiative is off track
entry.summary: Prepare a decision-ready account of delays, causes, options, and ownership.
prerequisites: Provide the executive ask, project tracker, metrics, financial context, meeting notes, and owner updates.
entry.outcome: An off-track brief with supported causes and clear decision options.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Explain why [initiative] is off track using the supplied documents, tracker, metrics, financial model, and recent owner updates. Establish what changed and when. Separate confirmed execution gaps from likely causes that still need testing. Compare recovery options, costs, timing, risks, dependencies, and accountable owners. State the specific decision leadership needs to make and cite material figures. Flag missing confirmation and return the brief for review without changing the tracker or sending it.

steps.title: Prepare the decision meeting
steps.prompt: Create a short discussion guide around the recovery options. Lead with the decision, show the key tradeoffs, and identify which owner must resolve each remaining uncertainty.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after reviewing the first result.

entry.title: Plan a behavior-preserving refactor
entry.summary: Break structural cleanup into small passes with explicit parity checks.
prerequisites: Provide the repository, refactor goals, supported public contracts, and validation commands.
entry.outcome: A staged refactor plan that separates cleanup from migrations and behavior changes.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Inspect this codebase for dead code, duplicated logic, oversized modules, stale abstractions, and legacy patterns that make changes difficult. Propose small reviewable refactor passes. For each, describe the existing behavior, the structural improvement, and the check that will establish parity. Preserve public APIs and user-visible behavior. Separate framework migrations, dependency upgrades, and architecture changes into their own decisions. For broad work, identify the specifications and compatibility checks needed before implementation. Return the plan first.

entry.title: Adopt Liquid Glass in one iOS flow
entry.summary: Use native visual treatments while preserving a usable fallback.
prerequisites: Requires an iOS app, Xcode 26 or compatible tooling, an iOS 26 simulator, and the chosen flow.
entry.outcome: A focused visual migration with earlier-OS fallback and simulator evidence.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Migrate [high-traffic SwiftUI flow] to native Liquid Glass. Audit existing backgrounds, blur layers, controls, sheets, and toolbars; distinguish interactive chrome from content that should remain plain. Prefer native glass APIs and system controls, keep shapes consistent, and use morphing or interactive effects only where the behavior warrants them. Preserve an availability-gated fallback for earlier supported iOS versions. Build and run the flow in the selected simulator, capture comparison screenshots, and report the scheme, OS, checks, and remaining visual issues.

entry.title: Scaffold a desktop-native macOS app
entry.summary: Set up Mac scenes, commands, and a simple local build-and-run workflow.
prerequisites: Requires macOS, Xcode or Swift tooling, and the app brief or existing project.
entry.outcome: A runnable Mac app slice with reusable development commands.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Create or extend a SwiftUI macOS app for [purpose]. Choose a main-window scene and add Settings, menu-bar, or utility windows only when they serve the workflow. Prefer native sidebars, menus, toolbars, keyboard shortcuts, and system materials. Use xcodebuild for an Xcode project or swift build for a package-based app and add a project-local build-and-run script. Keep AppKit bridging narrow and explain its need. Exercise the feature after each meaningful change and return exact verification commands and desktop-specific follow-ups.

entry.title: Reproduce and fix an iOS simulator bug
entry.summary: Observe the actual failing interaction before changing the code.
prerequisites: Provide the bug report, Xcode project, simulator access, and safe account or fixture setup.
entry.outcome: A reproduced issue, minimal fix, and evidence from the repeated simulator flow.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Investigate [bug] in this iOS app. Confirm the project, scheme, simulator, and required fixture before starting. Build and launch the app, inspect the current screen, and execute the reported taps, typing, scrolling, or swipes. Prefer accessibility identifiers and refresh the UI snapshot when layout changes. Capture screenshots, logs, and relevant debugger evidence. Diagnose the cause before making the smallest fix, then repeat the same interaction path. Report the reproduction, code change, environment, and verification gaps.

entry.title: Expose useful iOS actions to the system
entry.summary: Add a focused set of App Intents, entities, and shortcuts.
prerequisites: Provide the iOS app, target system versions, and the actions users should invoke outside the app.
entry.outcome: A tested first set of intents and clear routing into the app.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Audit [iOS app] for the most useful actions to expose through Shortcuts, Siri, Spotlight, widgets, or controls. Choose a small first set of actions and define only the entities needed to describe and route them. Add understandable titles, phrases, and display names. Distinguish actions that can run directly from those that should open a particular screen. Wire the scene handoff cleanly, preserve existing permissions, and build and test the supported paths. Explain which system experiences now work and which require later work.

entry.title: Make a Mac feature observable
entry.summary: Instrument meaningful state transitions without exposing sensitive data.
prerequisites: Provide the macOS repository, target feature, and access to run the app and inspect unified logs.
entry.outcome: Focused OSLog instrumentation and an observed event timeline.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Add lightweight unified logging to [Mac feature] using Logger from OSLog. Choose a clear subsystem and category. Record meaningful action boundaries and state transitions, with stable info messages and debug-level details only where needed. Exclude credentials, personal data, and document contents. Build and exercise the feature, then verify the event sequence with a focused Console or log-stream filter. If necessary, capture a small local trace for an intermittent flow. Return the filter, event timeline, representative evidence, and any missing transition that still needs investigation.

entry.title: Migrate a legacy codebase in checkpoints
entry.summary: Map compatibility risks before changing the stack.
prerequisites: Provide the current and target stacks, repository, public contracts, and build/test requirements.
entry.outcome: An incremental migration with tested checkpoints and rollback options.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Plan the migration from [legacy stack] to [target stack] in this repository. Inventory routing, data models, authentication, configuration, build tooling, tests, deployment, and external contracts. Map each existing capability to its target equivalent and highlight gaps. Define small milestones with compatibility layers and rollback options where needed. Preserve behavior unless a change is explicitly required. At each implemented checkpoint, run the relevant type, lint, and focused tests and resolve failures before continuing. Start by presenting the migration map and checkpoint plan.

entry.title: Create a custom security-review workflow
entry.summary: Run repeatable reviews on chosen triggers and retain their evidence.
prerequisites: Provide the repository, current scanner documentation, approved runner, secret-store setup, and desired triggers.
entry.outcome: A reviewable CI workflow that preserves reports and uses limited permissions.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Draft a GitHub Actions security-review workflow for [repository] using the currently supported scanner integration. Support [manual or scheduled triggers], use an explicit reviewed revision, and keep checkout credentials and job permissions limited to what the scan needs. Reference secrets through the CI secret store. Preserve readable findings, machine-readable results, and coverage evidence, including failed runs. Explain any SARIF requirements and artifact-access implications. Validate the workflow structure and provide the controlled first-run procedure before enabling it.

entry.title: Review security from the command line
entry.summary: Choose the right revision and scope, then inspect both findings and coverage.
prerequisites: Requires an authorized local checkout, installed security CLI, authentication, and repository security documents.
entry.outcome: A reproducible local review with exact scope and evidence locations.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Prepare a command-line security review of [working changes, branch diff, or selected component]. Verify the intended checkout and full revisions. For a branch review, compare the proposed head to its merge base; for local work, include only the intended staged and unstaged changes. Supply the repository policy and architecture context. Keep a selected-path assessment separate from a diff review, and include consumers of changed shared code where needed. Run the approved command, then inspect the manifest, findings, and coverage. Report commands, target revisions, unresolved alerts, and incomplete areas.

entry.title: Add security scanning to a delivery pipeline
entry.summary: Match scan scope to the trigger and handle incomplete runs explicitly.
prerequisites: Provide CI platform, repository, approved scan access, runner constraints, and cost/retention requirements.
entry.outcome: A staged scanning plan and pipeline change with evidence retention and clear enforcement behavior.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Add security scanning to [CI pipeline]. Start with [trigger]: scan the committed merge-base-to-head diff for pull requests, or the full specified revision for default-branch and scheduled runs. Use a trusted runner and isolate secrets from untrusted code. Set practical runtime and estimated cost limits, preserve reports and coverage artifacts, and verify the scanned revision. Begin with review-only reporting; propose blocking thresholds separately. Treat failed or incomplete scans as unresolved, even with no findings. Return a reviewable configuration and evidence from the approved validation run.

entry.title: Audit consistency across course sections
entry.summary: Separate required alignment from legitimate instructor choices.
prerequisites: Provide section syllabi, assignments, schedules, outcomes, LMS exports, and department guidance.
entry.outcome: A faculty review checklist of evidence-backed inconsistencies and priorities.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Compare the supplied sections of [course]. Check syllabi, assessment requirements, schedules, outcomes, and student instructions against department guidance. Distinguish required common standards from areas where instructors have discretion. Identify student-facing conflicts, cite the source for each, and rank them by urgency and impact. entry.outcome: An event playbook with public copy, private checklists, and open decisions.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Prepare a playbook for [event] from the named planning threads, approved documents, templates, and deadlines. Separate attendee-facing information from the private operating checklist. Include responsibilities, support resources, approvals still needed, open questions, and a source appendix. Check dates, locations, owners, and instructions against the supplied evidence. steps.title: Maintain the playbook

entry.title: Design tools for a conversational app
entry.summary: Define a small MCP tool surface around one user outcome.
prerequisites: Provide the use case, repository, target assistant platform, and current official integration documentation.
entry.outcome: A tool plan, proposed structure, test prompts, and integration requirements.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Plan a conversational app for [one core user outcome] in this repository. Consult the target platform's current official integration guidance. Propose three to five clearly named tools with precise descriptions, inputs, outputs, and authorization needs. Decide whether the first version needs an interactive widget or can return data alone. Prefer a TypeScript MCP server and React when a widget is justified. Return the tool plan, proposed file structure, representative test prompts, deployment and authentication requirements, risks, and unresolved decisions.

steps.title: Test the tool contract
steps.prompt: Create a small set of realistic user prompts that exercise each tool, ambiguous requests, unavailable data, and permission failures. Check whether the tool descriptions and results make the correct behavior clear.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after reviewing the first result.

entry.title: Audit a manual workflow
entry.summary: Find the bottlenecks and define two narrow automation opportunities.
prerequisites: Provide tracker, process documentation, handoff notes, tickets, metrics, and operational constraints.
entry.outcome: A workflow audit, revised process draft, and two focused automation specifications.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Audit [workflow] before [deadline]. Reconstruct its steps and owners from the tracker, documentation, handoff notes, tickets, metrics, and discussions. Identify stuck points, repeated questions, missing data, and conflicting or stale instructions. Draft an updated process description and a small automation specification for the two most repetitive manual steps. Explain inputs, outputs, exceptions, and human decisions. Keep recommendations bounded and do not implement or publish process changes.

steps.title: Select the first automation
steps.prompt: Compare the two automation candidates by frequency, effort, dependencies, failure impact, and available evidence. Recommend the smallest useful first release and define how to verify that it helps.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after reviewing the first result.
