steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Create the first campaign kit for [launch] from the supplied plan, product notes, tracker, creative brief, page links, and approval rules. Include a launch-review brief, customer email, internal announcement, social post, two-week content calendar, creative or agency brief, staging-page fixes, and a team update. Keep the central message and facts consistent across formats. Flag unsupported claims, missing assets, and product or legal approval needs. Do not send or publish any draft.

steps.title: Check launch readiness

entry.title: Investigate an incident and prove the fix
entry.summary: Use isolated reproduction and before-and-after evidence to avoid speculative patches.
prerequisites: Provide a sanitized incident packet, affected revision, safe fixtures, approved test commands, and an isolated environment.
entry.outcome: A supported incident investigation, focused patch where justified, and evidence-based handoff.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Investigate [incident] in [repository] using the sanitized packet. Confirm the affected revision and environment, read repository instructions, and build a sourced timeline. Separate observations, hypotheses, and evidence gaps. Reproduce the strongest hypothesis in the isolated test environment; if evidence is insufficient, return the next diagnostic step instead of a speculative fix. For a confirmed defect, demonstrate a failing regression test, make the smallest patch, and rerun focused and broader checks. Record commands, exit codes, revisions, and limitations. Return a diff, local draft PR description, test evidence, and rollout/rollback notes. Do not access or modify production, replay live events, post updates, merge, or deploy.

steps.title: Investigate duplicate webhook processing
steps.instruction: Use this follow-up only when the incident involves duplicate webhook deliveries.
steps.prompt: For this duplicate-webhook incident, test failures both before and after commit and reproduce contention with independent database connections. Document transaction isolation, receipt retention, and mixed-version rollout assumptions. Before resuming retained deliveries, identify legacy orders without matching receipts after old consumers drain. Keep unresolved event keys held through the existing quarantine process. Add an orphan-with-pending-retry case proving that no second order or success acknowledgment occurs while held. Reconcile only from trusted immutable event identity, canonical payload, and committed-order evidence; do not invent fingerprints, delete receipts, or replay unresolved live events.

entry.title: Migrate a validation module without contract drift
entry.summary: Compare the same public contract before and after a bounded dependency change.
prerequisites: Provide the module, pinned baseline/target versions, migration guide, callers, frozen contract tests, and isolated environment.
entry.outcome: A scoped migration with before-and-after contract evidence and rollback notes.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Migrate [validation module] from [pinned baseline] to [approved target] within [scope]. Record the starting revision, runtime and dependency versions, and lockfile hash. Read the official guide, callers, public contracts, and repository instructions; run the baseline first. Keep broader dependency preparation separate. Run the same frozen HTTP contract tests through the real router and serialization before and after the change, comparing statuses, headers, accepted inputs, defaults, nulls, JSON shapes, and full errors. Do not weaken assertions or approve new snapshots to hide differences. Return the diff, exact validation evidence, unresolved incompatibilities, and rollback plan without merging or deploying.

entry.title: Build a hackathon event hub
entry.summary: Keep the agenda, team registration, submissions, and project gallery connected.
prerequisites: Provide event brief, agenda, time zone, team rules, deadlines, visibility rules, and an authenticated app environment.
entry.outcome: A private event site with persistent team submissions and tested membership controls.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Build a private site for [hackathon] from the supplied brief, agenda, rules, and resources. Confirm conflicting times or missing deadline policies first. Include event information, agenda, participant instructions, organizer contact, team registration, project drafts/submission, and a gallery governed by the approved visibility rule. Require sign-in and verified team membership; enforce own-team editing on the server. Keep agenda data separate from registrations and projects so updates preserve submissions. Validate required fields and demo links. Test two fictional teams, reload persistence, direct cross-team access, deadline behavior, and mobile layout. Remove test records and show the reviewed preview before publishing.

steps.title: Update the agenda safely
steps.prompt: Apply [approved agenda change] while preserving registrations, project drafts, submissions, and their access rules. Recheck the event time zone and deadline display and report exactly what changed.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after reviewing the first result.

entry.title: Build a first-week onboarding portal
entry.summary: Guide new hires through sourced tasks while keeping individual progress private.
prerequisites: Provide the approved first-week plan, resources, contacts, practice task, and an authenticated app environment.
entry.outcome: A private portal with persistent checklists, practice instructions, and verified progress isolation.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Build an onboarding portal for [role] from the approved first-week plan. Include daily tasks, resources, contacts, and the end-of-week practice task. Show each task's purpose, completion criteria, source link, and support contact; use time estimates only when supplied. Preserve the plan's sequence and add progress and resume controls. Require sign-in, keep progress private to its owner with server-side enforcement, and use stable task IDs so content updates do not erase completion. Treat progress as activity completion, not job-readiness scoring. Test two accounts, partial and completed plans, reloads, and instruction edits. Show a private preview before sharing.

steps.title: Refresh the task content
steps.prompt: Update the portal from [approved revised plan]. Preserve task identities and existing completion records where the task is unchanged, flag meaningful scope changes, and recheck resource permissions and progress privacy.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after reviewing the first result.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Build a creative request app for [team] using its approved brief template. Capture audience, message, format, requested date, reviewer, and reference links; keep the requested date distinct from the team's agreed delivery date. Give each request its brief, owner, status, current draft, feedback, and final asset, using New, In progress, In review, and Delivered. Add filters for owner, status, and agreed date. Require sign-in; enforce requester access to their own records and creative-team management rights on the server. Save feedback across visits. entry.title: Compare campaign spending and lead generation
entry.summary: Use consistent filters and weighted calculations to explain campaign performance.
prerequisites: Provide campaign-by-week data, reporting period, currency, time zone, lead definition, and attribution rules.
entry.outcome: A validated dashboard with source-row drilldown and an explicit refresh process.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Build a private campaign dashboard from [file or exact sheet tab]. Inspect row counts, dates, campaign IDs, duplicates, currencies, missing values, and mapping gaps first. Show spend, leads, cost per lead, weekly trends, and campaign comparisons using the same filtered rows throughout. Compute cost per lead as total spend divided by total leads, not an average of row ratios; use N/A for zero leads. Keep missing values distinct from zero and currencies separate without an approved conversion rule. Include source-row drilldown and a safe export-refresh process. Validate totals, filters, duplicates, partial weeks, and mobile layout. Do not infer revenue or lead quality from lead counts.

steps.title: Compare consecutive periods
steps.prompt: Compare [two periods] using consistent definitions and complete-week boundaries. Explain which campaigns drove changes in spend, leads, and aggregate cost per lead, and flag data coverage that limits the comparison.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after reviewing the first result.

entry.summary: Summarize actual progress and next priorities from work evidence.
prerequisites: Provide the reporting week and approved calendar, documents, messages, and project tracker sources.
entry.outcome: A concise unsent update with source-linked outcomes, blockers, and priorities.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Draft my update for [week] using the relevant calendar events, edited documents, sent messages, and project tracker. Focus on completed work, decisions, material changes, blockers, follow-ups, and next week's priorities. Link evidence where useful and distinguish confirmed outcomes from inferred progress. Keep the language concise and appropriate for [manager or audience]. Do not inflate activity into impact or include unrelated private context. Return the draft without sending or publishing it.

steps.title: Prepare next week
steps.prompt: Extract the commitments and open follow-ups from this update into a short review checklist for next week. Keep proposed priorities distinct from work already agreed with the team.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after reviewing the first result.

entry.title: Turn an issue into a tested code change
entry.summary: Tie implementation and review evidence directly to acceptance criteria.
prerequisites: Provide issue, acceptance criteria, exact baseline revision, scoped files, fixtures, and required checks in a prepared environment.
entry.outcome: A minimal diff or authorized draft PR with an acceptance-evidence table.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Implement [issue] in [repository] from [base commit] within [scope]. Read the instructions, relevant code, acceptance criteria, and public contracts. Confirm the revision and run baseline checks; report blocking failures or missing access before implementation. Make the smallest change using existing authorization, error, pagination, and test patterns. Add regression tests that distinguish the new behavior from the old. Run required checks again and map every criterion to actual evidence, with commands, results, revisions, and unrun checks. Return the diff and draft review description, or create a draft PR only when authorized. Do not merge, deploy, alter production, add dependencies, or expand scope without a decision.

steps.title: Verify a cursor-pagination change
steps.instruction: Use this follow-up when the issue changes cursor pagination.
steps.prompt: Verify the pagination contract with fixed fixtures, including tied timestamps across a page boundary, bounded traversal, repeatable cursor replay, and both partial and exactly full final pages. Confirm authorization happens before cursor validation, cover malformed or invalid cursors, and compare successful and error responses with the public schemas. Keep existing assertions strong and update API documentation to match the actual contract. Report any unrun check or unresolved difference explicitly.
